references.text: The prophecy that the Messiah would shed his blood for many, which foretells Jesus' sacrifice.
Reference to the new covenant that God would establish, where Jesus' blood becomes the definitive sacrifice.
Matthew's version of the institution of the Lord's Supper, where Jesus refers to his blood as the covenant poured out for many.
Luke's account of the Lord's Supper, which also highlights Jesus' blood as the new covenant poured out for many.
Reference to Jesus' blood as the foundation of the new covenant, in line with what Jesus said during the Last Supper.
Compares Jesus' sacrifice with that of Abel, and emphasizes the importance of Jesus' blood as the foundation of the new covenant.
